B3L01-G01-P29: 可以說是 means you could say it is. It explains or sums up what was just said, and 可說是 means the same.
It does not mean being able to speak. For that, use 可以說 without 是.
For plain facts like who someone is, use ordinary 是.
B3L01-G02-P30: 多麼 ... 啊 shows strong feeling that something is more than expected, in an exaggerated tone.
麼 can be left out, and 啊 goes at the end of the sentence.
多麼 goes before an adjective, not directly before a noun.
It can't ask about price or amount. Use 多少 for that.
B3L01-G03-P32: 再說 adds one more reason or a fuller explanation to what was just said.
Put 再說 at the start of the added sentence, never at the very end.
To ask someone to say it again, use 請再說一次, not 再說 alone.
B3L01-G04-P38: 而 links a cause to its result, mostly in writing or formal speech.
因為 comes before the reason and 而 before the result, so 因為……而…… means 因為……所以…….
Don't use 而 between two nouns. Use 和 or 跟 for nouns.
B3L01-G05-P40: Put 出 after a verb to say that the action makes something new appear.
Common verbs are 想, 做, 說, 寫 and 畫.
This is not 出 for moving out of a place, which uses 走出來.
B3L01-G06-P42: 就算 means even if. The imagined situation after it does not change the facts or the decision.
Use 也 in the second part, not 但是.
雖然 starts a real fact, but 就算 starts an imagined condition.
B3L02-G01-P51: 早就……了 says the speaker feels something happened a long time ago.
已經 only says it is done. 早就 adds the feeling of long ago.
Don't use it for something that just happened. Use 剛才 or 剛剛 instead.
B3L02-G02-P52: 順便 means you do a second thing while doing the first, without much extra trouble or time.
It is often used when asking someone to do a small extra thing.
Put 順便 right before the second verb. For a special trip, say 特地 or 專門.
B3L02-G03-P53: 一會兒……，一會兒…… says two or more situations happen one after the other or take turns.
The speaker feels the change is quick, and the tone is sometimes a little exaggerated.
Say both parts. For two actions at the same time, use 一邊……一邊…….
B3L02-G04-P54: 算了 is a spoken way to say forget it: you are unhappy but won't spend more time or effort.
It can be a whole sentence by itself, or come after a different choice, as in 我找別人跟我去算了.
To say you finished calculating, use 算好了, not 算了.
B3L02-G05-P62: 開 after a verb is the result of the action. It means things that were together come apart.
It can also mean a person or thing leaves where it was. 走不開 means you are too busy to leave.
Put 得 or 不 between the verb and 開 to say can or can't, as in 打不開.
B3L02-G06-P64: 經過 can be followed by a stretch of past time, as in 經過了兩個小時.
It can also be followed by a process that happened, as in 經過李老闆修理.
The sentence then gives the result. Don't put an adjective right after 經過.
B3L02-G07-P65: 用 plus a tool or method says how you do something.
Put the tool or method first, then the action.
來 can be left out and the meaning stays the same.
B3L03-G01-P78: 試 plus a verb means to try it first, before you decide to buy or use something.
The verb is usually one syllable, such as 吃, 穿, 用, 喝 or 開.
Use 試 once, as in 試躺. Don't say 試試躺.
B3L03-G02-P80: 掉 after a verb with an object means getting rid of something or a bad result, as in 吃掉.
After a verb with no object, 掉 means leaving, as in 走掉 and 跑掉.
完 means finishing. 掉 means throwing away, using up, or a bad result.
B3L03-G03-P81: 什麼(N)都 means all or any, as in 他什麼忙都幫: he helps with anything.
就是 then names the only choice or the one different case.
他什麼茶都喝，就是不喝紅茶 means he drinks any tea except black tea.
B3L03-G04-P82: 別再……了 is for telling or reminding someone else to stop doing something.
不再……了 is for your own decision, or for saying that someone no longer does something.
B3L03-G05-P88: 不僅 means the same as 不但, and it is mostly used in writing.
The second part starts with 還, 也 or 而且 to add more.
Don't use 但是 after 不僅.
B3L03-G06-P90: This pattern says a degree changes step by step, as in 一天比一天熱了.
Put 比 between the two measure words, then the adjective.
Don't drop 比: 一樣一樣 only shows things one after another, with no comparison.
B3L04-G01-P101: 好 plus an adjective plus 的 plus a noun is a strong exclamation, as in 好有趣的表演啊.
You must keep 的 between the adjective and the noun.
Use 好, not 很, to make this exclamation.
B3L04-G02-P103: V 來 V 去，還是…… says someone did an action again and again, spent time, and nothing changed.
After 還是, the speaker gives an opinion, a feeling or a decision.
想來想去 shows long thinking before the answer. 想想 is only a short thought.
B3L04-G03-P105: 終於 means finally: after a long process, a hoped-for result comes.
Put it after the subject and before the verb or adjective. Add 了 at the end to show a change.
終於 shows relief after hard effort or a long wait. 最後 only says what came last.
B3L04-G04-P113: V個不停 says the same action keeps repeating in a short time, as in 雨下個不停.
V個沒完 says the action can't or won't stop, and usually the speaker feels annoyed or impatient.
If the verb has an object, say the verb twice: 開會開個不停.
B3L04-G05-P114: 不 Vs₁ 不 Vs₂ says something is in the middle and just right, as in 不大不小.
Both words must be one syllable and opposites, such as 多少, 高矮 and 冷熱.
B3L04-G06-P115: 除了……就是…… says that if you take away the first thing, only the second is left.
以外 can be left out.
除了……也/還…… adds one more thing. 除了……就是…… leaves only one.
B3L04-G07-P117: 不是……，就是…… says it must be one of two things, with no other choice.
Don't use it when both are true at once.
除了……就是…… is different: it takes one thing away and says only the other is left.
B3L05-G01-P128: 萬一 is followed by something very unlikely to happen, usually something bad.
After the 萬一 part, 就 gives the bad result and 才 gives a way to avoid trouble.
如果 and 要是 work for any normal condition. 萬一 is only for unlikely events.
B3L05-G02-P130: 一連 says the same action or situation happens again and again without a break.
It is followed by a verb or a number with a measure word, as in 一連三天.
Put 不 or 沒 after the number phrase, right before the verb.
B3L05-G03-P132: 以為 is followed by what the speaker first believed, which was wrong.
沒想到 is followed by what really happened, which the speaker never expected.
Use 以為, not 認為 or 覺得, when the first belief turned out wrong.
B3L05-G04-P133: After comparing the choices, the speaker gives a conclusion or advice. The advice comes after 還是.
吧 at the end makes the advice softer, like a friendly suggestion, not a command.
B3L05-G05-P141: 結果 connects an event to the final situation after it.
所以 gives a logical result. 結果 gives how things finally ended, often not what was hoped.
結果 can also be a noun that means the outcome, as in 考試的結果.
B3L05-G06-P143: 甚至 is followed by the person, thing or case the speaker wants to stress.
It is often used with 不但 or 連……都/也…….
而且 adds a similar point. 甚至 adds a more extreme case. If you use 連, put it right after 甚至.
B3L05-G07-P144: 以 marks a boundary. Put a place name before it, then a direction after it.
臺中以北 means the area north of 臺中. The directions are 以東, 以西, 以南 and 以北.
B3L06-G01-P155: 倒是 agrees with the other person in a polite way, then 可是, 但是 or 不過 gives a different view.
倒 can be left out, so 是 alone works.
Put the agreeing part first and 可是 after it. 可能是 only guesses, it doesn't agree.
B3L06-G02-P157: X分之Y says a part of a whole, as in 三分之二, which means two out of three.
The whole comes first, before 分之, and the part comes after it.
For percent, say 百分之五. Don't leave out 分.
B3L06-G03-P159: 總算 says something you hoped for finally happened after a wait or hard work.
It is often used in speech.
Use it for something that already happened. 總是 means always, not finally.
B3L06-G04-P160: 既然 starts with a fact that already happened or is sure.
就 comes in the second part and gives the speaker's opinion, advice or conclusion.
如果 sets up a maybe, but 既然 starts from a fact.
B3L06-G05-P167: 在……中 means in a certain situation or area, as in 在我的生活中.
Put the noun phrase between 在 and 中. Keep both, and don't use 裡 here.
B3L06-G06-P169: 不能不 means you must do it, because you should be responsible for it.
不得不 means you don't want to, but have no choice, so you feel helpless.
不得不 sounds stronger than 不能不.
B3L06-G07-P171: 正 means by coincidence: the first thing is just starting or about to start, and a second thing happens then.
正 is often followed by 要, 想, 打算 or 準備, and 就 starts the second part.
Use 正要, not 正在, for just about to.
B3L07-G01-P184: 才……就…… shows surprise that a short time or small amount already gives a result, as in 才吃一碗就飽了.
才 can also mean just now, and the 就 part happens right after it, as in 我才出門就下雨了.
剛……就…… only says it just happened, without the surprise.
B3L07-G02-P186: Use 話說回來 when you don't oppose what the other person said but have a different or better idea.
It can also bring the talk back to the topic and give your main opinion.
Put 不過, 可是 or 但是 before it.
B3L07-G03-P187: 這麼說 means going by what the other person just said.
The speaker then gives their own guess drawn from it.
這麼說 starts the reply. 也就是說 is different: it restates the same meaning in other words.
B3L07-G04-P189: 成 after a verb is the result of the action and means it succeeded or was done.
V 成 means it was done. 沒 V 成 means it didn't get done, for something that already happened.
V 得成 and V 不成 say it is possible or not possible to get done.
B3L07-G05-P195: 就……來說 looks at one thing or one area to describe or analyze it, mostly in writing.
對……來說 gives one person's view. 就……來說 looks at a topic or standard.
Keep 來說 in the pattern. Don't use 看 in its place.
B3L07-G06-P197: 得 comes after a verb or adjective, and what follows tells how far the action or state goes.
What follows 得 can be an exaggerated word or a short sentence.
Use 得, not 的, for this.
B3L08-G01-P210: 把 plus the first noun, verb, 成 and the second noun says someone turns one thing into another.
把旅行的經驗寫成一本書 means turning travel experiences into a book.
After 看, 聽, 說, 寫 or 念, 成 sometimes means you got it wrong, as in 看成.
B3L08-G02-P211: 再……，也/都…… takes a situation to the extreme, and the result or decision stays the same.
It means almost the same as 就算……，也……, and the speaker may feel the action is right and worth doing.
Use 再, not 更 or 又, as in 再辛苦也要忍耐.
B3L08-G03-P213: 慣 after a verb means used to it, as the result of doing it.
Add 得 or 不 to say you can or can't get used to it: 住得慣 and 吃不慣.
Say 吃不慣, not 吃不習慣了.
B3L08-G04-P219: 況且 adds a further reason after the main reason, to make the reasoning fuller.
It often goes with 也, 還 or 又.
Put 況且 before the second reason, not the first. Use 況且, not 但是.
B3L08-G05-P221: 非……不可 means you must do something and have no other choice.
非 means 不, and a verb or verb phrase comes after it.
Put 非 before the whole action, as in 非向他道歉不可, and 不可 at the end.
B3L08-G06-P222: 畢竟 is followed by a conclusion after thinking, which gives the key point of the matter.
The speaker uses it to remind or persuade the other person.
Put 畢竟 before the key point, not after it. 究竟 doesn't work here.
B3L09-G01-P235: 過來 after a verb can mean coming back to the normal or original state, as in 醒過來.
過去 is the opposite: from a normal state to a bad one, as in 暈過去. It is used less.
忙不過來 means there is too much work to handle.
B3L09-G02-P237: 怎麼不……反而……呢 asks why someone didn't do what is expected and did something else instead.
After 怎麼不, put what the speaker thinks should be done.
After 反而, put what should not be done, or what the speaker doubts.
B3L09-G03-P238: 不但不 or 不但沒 is followed by something opposite to what the speaker expected.
反而 then gives something surprising, or something the speaker thinks should not happen.
Sometimes 不但 can be left out.
B3L09-G04-P240: 才 stresses what comes after it, and is often used to argue against what someone said.
The sentence often ends with 呢.
Put 才 before what you stress, such as 不 or 沒: 我才不要呢.
B3L09-G05-P247: 尤其 means especially. It shows one thing is more special than the others.
It usually goes in the second sentence.
尤其是 picks out one thing from a group, as in 五門課都很有意思，尤其是英文會話課.
B3L09-G06-P248: 著 after a verb says whether the action reached its goal or result, like 找著了.
The verb must aim at a goal, such as 拿, 看, 打, 猜, 用 or 找.
Put 得 or 不 before 著 to say you can or can't reach it.
B3L09-G07-P250: 以 means 用. 以……代替…… means using one thing or action in place of the original.
Put the new thing after 以 and the old thing after 代替.
B3L10-G01-P262: 直到……才…… says something that had not happened until a certain time finally happened.
After 直到 put the time or situation. After 才 put the result.
才 shows the speaker thinks the result came later than expected.
B3L10-G02-P263: 只不過 adds a note to what was said, so the listener understands the situation better.
It means 只是. Put the added explanation after it.
B3L10-G03-P265: 害 is like 讓 or 使 but stronger. It says something causes a bad result for someone.
Put the cause before 害, then the person affected, then the bad result.
B3L10-G04-P272: 到底 after a verb stresses carrying something through to the end, with effort.
Put 到底 after the verb: say 堅持到底, not 到底堅持.
B3L10-G05-P274: 一再 says an action or event happens again and again.
Put it after the subject and before the verb.
B3L10-G06-P275: 假如, 如果 and 要是 all set up a condition. The result often follows with 就.
假如 goes before the subject and is mostly used in writing.
如果 works in writing or speech. 要是 works only in speech. Both can go before or after the subject.
B3L10-G07-P276: 為了……而…… says what someone does to reach a goal.
The part after 為了 is the goal. The part after 而 is what is done to reach it.
B3L11-G01-P289: 透過 says a person, thing or action is the way a result is reached.
Put what you went through after 透過, then the action.
Use 透過, not 經過 or 通過, for this meaning.
B3L11-G02-P291: 以上 means more than or higher than a point, and it includes that point. 六十分以上 includes 六十分.
以下 means lower than a point, or not reaching it.
以 with a direction word, as in 以內, 以外, 以北 or 以南, marks a range.
B3L11-G03-P292: 看得起 means you think the other person is important. 看不起 means you look down on them.
Don't mix it up with V得起 and V不起, which say whether someone can afford something.
B3L11-G04-P299: 卻 shows something is the opposite of the facts or of what was expected, as in 他卻沒來.
Put it after the subject and before the verb.
B3L11-G05-P301: 對得起 means you did nothing wrong, so you didn't disappoint, anger or embarrass the other person.
Put the person or thing after it, as in 對不起朋友.
B3L11-G06-P302: 至於 moves to another topic or view that connects to the first topic.
Put the new topic after 至於, then say what you think about it.
B3L12-G01-P313: 這就 says you will do something right now, on the spot.
這 means 現在 and 就 means immediately. Put a verb or verb phrase after it.
Don't use it for later times: you can't say 明天這就.
B3L12-G02-P314: 在……方面 names the area you are talking about, and the rest says what is true there.
Put the area between 在 and 方面. Keep both words.
對……來說 gives a point of view, not an area. Don't say 對穿著方面.
B3L12-G03-P316: 往往 says something tends to happen under certain conditions, as a pattern seen again and again.
Use it for what has already happened or for general facts, not for plans or personal wishes.
Always say both characters, and never put 不 before it: no 不往往.
常常 also means it happens often, but 往往 has more limits.
B3L12-G04-P318: 有關 usually starts a sentence to bring up a topic. The next part explains it or gives advice.
It can also describe a noun: 跟……有關的資料.
對於 gives the speaker's view of the object, but 有關 only brings up the topic.
B3L12-G05-P325: 儘管 means about the same as 雖然. It starts the first part and states a fact.
The second part often uses 可是, 但是, 還是 or 卻 to show the opposite result.
儘管 is for facts that already happened. 即使 is for an imagined situation.
B3L12-G06-P327: 不論……都…… shows that the result stays the same even when the situation changes.
After 不論 put a question word, a pair of opposites like 大小, or an A not A question.
After 都 put the result or fact that will surely happen.
既然……就 is different: it says what naturally follows from something already true.
B3L13-G01-P338: 這下子 gives the speaker's view of a situation just mentioned, or a reaction to something sudden.
It stresses the immediate result of what just happened. 現在 only states the time now.
B3L13-G02-P339: 既……又…… says the same subject has two states or situations.
Both must be good or both must be bad.
Don't put an adverb like 很 before the adjectives.
The state after 又 is a little stronger, and this pattern is used more in writing than 又……又…….
B3L13-G03-P341: 更別說 means there is no need to say it, because the case after it is so clear.
First give the easier or basic case, often with 連……都, then 更別說 and the harder one.
B3L13-G04-P347: 就是……也…… means even if. The imagined situation after 就是 does not change the result after 也.
In speech it works like 即使……也…….
只要……就 is different: it says if A happens, B must follow.
B3L13-G05-P348: 一方面……一方面…… gives two sides of one matter, such as two reasons, results or purposes.
The two parts are equal. Neither is more important.
不但……而且…… is different: the second part goes a step further.
B3L14-G01-P360: 就要從……說起了 says something is hard to explain simply, so you must start from one angle, part or time.
Change 說 to a one-syllable verb like 看, 做 or 聊, not a longer one like 說明.
End with 起了, not 起來. If the topic was already mentioned, leave out 這 or 那.
B3L14-G02-P362: 下去 after a verb shows that an action keeps going.
No object can come after V下去.
得 means you can keep going and 不 means you can't, as in 看不下去.
B3L14-G03-P363: 幸虧 introduces a lucky event that happened.
要不然 then gives the bad or worrying result that would have happened without it.
B3L14-G04-P369: 根據 means using something as the base for a judgment, action or conclusion.
After 根據 put a noun phrase for the basis, such as 報告, 調查, 經驗 or 法律.
根據 gives the reason behind a conclusion. 按照 is about how something is done.
B3L14-G05-P371: 按照 means doing something by a method, rule, plan or standard.
It stresses how something is done, as in 按照杯子大小算. You can shorten it to 按 or 照.
根據 stresses why you say or do something, and it can also be a noun.
B3L15-G01-P383: 簡直 describes something in an exaggerated, vivid way, to say it is almost like that.
It can be followed by 像, 就像, 是 or 就是.
簡直 is a vivid view from the speaker, not just a degree word like 很 or 非常.
B3L15-G02-P384: Put a describing word before 得沒話說 to say you can't find a better word for it.
It is mostly positive, for praise, not for criticism.
沒話說 can also stand alone, as in 服務沒話說, to mean nothing to complain about.
B3L15-G03-P392: 同時 as a noun or adverb means actions or events happen at the same time.
Between two sentences, it joins two equal ones and adds a further point.
一邊……一邊…… is for one person doing two actions at once. 同時 can also join two roles or further points.
B3L15-G04-P393: 及 joins nouns and means the same as 和 or 跟, but it is more formal.
It is mostly for writing. Don't use it to join whole sentences.
With three or more items, put 及 only between the last two.
B3L15-G05-P395: 總而言之 gives a short conclusion to what came before, without much detail.
It can be shortened to 總之.
Don't mix it up with 總算, which means finally, or 總共, which adds up amounts.
B3L16-G01-P404: 當作 means to treat one thing as if it were the same as another.
It can also show a judgment about something, such as 被人當作是學生.
With 把, the subject does the treating. With 被, the subject is the one treated that way.
B3L16-G02-P406: 至少 means at least: it shows the lowest amount or level.
After 至少 put a quantity or a short sentence.
It can also name the smallest step that must be done, as in 至少得先聽聽其他人的意見.
B3L16-G03-P413: 由於 gives the reason and 因此 gives the result. This is more formal than 因為……，所以…….
由於 usually starts the first part.
If the reason comes second, write 是由於, not just 由於.
B3L16-G04-P415: 使得 links a cause to the result it brings about.
It is like 使 but more formal.
使得 is often used for facts that already happened, and 使 for imagined situations.
B3L16-G05-P417: 於是 joins two sentences. The second shows an action taken because of the first.
Don't use it when the second part is a natural event, as in 於是下雨了. Use 所以 instead.
